drhp.business: GHL operates in a single Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) segment, undertaking construction, operations and maintenance of carriageways on toll and annuity basis pursuant to development agreements with the Central and State Governments. The company also makes investments in group companies engaged in road, highway, bridge, tunnel and toll-road construction and operation, and partners with BOT concessionaires for the EPC scope of projects.
drhp.end_markets: Indian national and state highways sector

litigation.note: Union Bank of India filed a Section 7 IBC application against Indore Dewas Tollways Limited (a material subsidiary); NCLT Hyderabad admitted the petition on 31/10/2023 and has since ordered liquidation, with IDTL still under liquidation (Board's Report / MD&A). Separately, Cyberabad Expressways Limited (a jointly controlled entity) has an arbitration/court dispute over dues from the Government of Telangana/HGCL/HMDA — the company states it has won in Arbitration, Commercial Court and two additional High Court cases, with a Section 37 petition still pending in the Telangana High Court and an Executive Petition pending in Commercial Court (BRSR / auditor qualification explanation).

The company operates in only one segment, Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT), concentrating its business and cash flows in one project model.
Revenue-generating activity flows from development agreements with the Central and State Governments, exposing the company to policy and counterparty risk from government bodies.

The company depends on the skills of executives, designers and engineers; loss of key employees could impair its ability to implement its business strategy, and continued ability to attract and retain qualified employees is not assured.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Government of India's continued focus on infrastructure development (Bharatmala Pariyojana, PM Gati Shakti, National Infrastructure Pipeline, National Monetisation Pipeline) is expected to support world-class infrastructure creation and connectivity.
- Roads and highways sector expected to continue growing on increased investment in construction, expansion and modernization of the national highway network.
- Union Budget 2026-27 infrastructure capital expenditure outlay increased, with government capital expenditure described as increasing 4.2 times to Rs.11.21 lakh crores in FY26, expected to strengthen roads, railways, ports and logistics growth.
- Proposed Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund and a dedicated pipeline for PPP-led projects and investment are expected to strengthen private-sector confidence in infrastructure development.
- Increasing adoption of technology-driven project management systems, digital monitoring, sustainable construction practices and enhanced safety standards expected to improve project execution and operational efficiency across the sector.
- Growing emphasis on green and resilient infrastructure expected to create opportunities for companies able to deliver projects aligned with evolving ESG expectations.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management states risk management by its nature is flawed because it identifies only known risks and fails to appreciate 'unknowns' and 'uncontrollables', which can leave project risks unaddressed.
- The company operates in only one segment, Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT), concentrating its business and cash flows in one project model.
- Revenue-generating activity flows from development agreements with the Central and State Governments, exposing the company to policy and counterparty risk from government bodies.
- The company depends on the skills of executives, designers and engineers; loss of key employees could impair its ability to implement its business strategy, and continued ability to attract and retain qualified employees is not assured.
- Persistent geopolitical tensions, evolving trade dynamics, inflationary pressures and commodity-price fluctuations create a mixed global growth environment that could affect operating conditions.
- Cautionary statement flags changes in government regulations, tax laws and economic/political developments within the country as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.
- Cautionary statement explicitly names litigations and industrial relations among factors that could materially affect operations.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to focus on opportunities by partnering with BOT concessionaires for the EPC scope of projects.
- Strengthen present projects and maintain the operating momentum built during FY2025-26.
- Remain focused on identifying and pursuing viable business opportunities while strengthening core competencies in project execution, operations and maintenance.
